located at the lower-most aspect of the rib cage. It serves two main functions: - Separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominal cavity (the word diaphragm is derived from the Greek ?diáphragma?, meaning partition). - Undergoes contraction and relaxation, altering the volume of the thoracic cavity and the lungs, producing inspiration and expiration. 1-The main orifices: -Aortic hiatus: -fibrous orifice. -It projects onto the body of T12 between the 2 main pillars. -Esophageal hiatus:-muscular orifice -It projects onto T10 to the left of the midline. -passage elements: esophagus and the vagus nerves -Foramen of the IVC:-fibrous orifice -It projects onto T9, to the right of the midline. -passage elements: IVC and abdominal branch of the right phrenic nerve. 2-Accessory orifices:

-Marfan's cleft: retro-sternal, between the 2 bundles of the sternal portion of the diaphragm. -Larrey's cleft: retro-sternal, lateral, between the 2 sternal and chondro-costal portions. Allows passage of the superior epigastric artery. -Medial hiatus: pre-lumbar, located between the main and accessory pillars. Allows passage of the greater splanchnic nerve. -Lateral hiatus: pre-lumbar, between the accessory pillar and the medial arcuate pillar. Allows the passage of the lesser splanchnic nerve and the lower splanchnic nerve and the sympathetic chain. It is the main inspiratory muscle, very powerful during inspiration, ? It increases by contracting the 3 diameters of the thorax: - Vertical: by lowering the torque, thanks to the costal fulcrum. - Sagittal: projecting the sternum forward. - Transverse: by elevating the ribs thanks to the point of support on the abdominal viscera. 2-Secondary roles: ? Suspends the supramesocolic and lumbar viscera. ? Promotes by contracting blood circulation, and lymph, the flow of bile,

vomiting. ? Acts on the esophageal orifice and opposes the reflux of gastric contents. ? Causes by its contraction the cry, yawning, and by its spasms, hiccups, laughter. ? Opposes the pelvic diaphragm (levator ani) in defecation, forced urination and
allows passage into the thoracic cavity of the esophageal junction and part of the stomach.

headers: A- The vessels of the thoracic face: 1-The arteries: they come from the subclavian artery, we distinguish: -The superior phrenic arteries. -The internal thoracic arteries. 2-The veins: they are superimposed on the arteries and go to the SVC -The right and left superior phrenic veins -The right and left internal thoracic veins 3-The lymphatics: the superior lymphatic network of the diaphragm drains through its lymphatic collectors towards the lymphatic nodes of the thorax.
rows: B- The vessels of the thoracic face: 1-The arteries: they come from the abdominal aorta, these are the lower phrenic arteries 2-The veins: these are the lower phrenic veins drain the abdominal sides of the diaphragmatic domes and end in the IVC. 3-The lymphatics: drains towards the lymph nodes in the abdominal region. diaphragm is often a difficult diagnosis. Options for diagnosis include laparoscopy, thoracoscopy or a CT scan. Irrespective of the size of the tear, the muscle must be repaired as soon as possible to prevent herniation of abdominal organs. ? The diaphragm is also involved in hiccups. When the muscle is irritated, it can result in sudden
contractions which can be uncomfortable. Most hiccups are short-lived, but in rare cases, hiccups may last for a day. If the hiccups persist, they can interfere with breathing.
